stops.name: Kalam
stops.caption: The metalled road ends here; a shingle road continues to the Ushu and Utror valleys.

stops.name: Matiltan
stops.caption: It is about 11 km from Kalam and Falak Sar can be seen from it.

stops.name: Ushu (Usho)
stops.caption: It is mainly inhabited by Gawri people. Mahodand Lake lies 27 km from the village.

stories.title: Kalam to Mahodand by road
stories.note: Waypoints are the sourced places in the upper pack; the camera follows the road and track lines in the map data between them.

stops.name: Kalam
stops.caption: It lies 99 km north of Mingora at about 2,000 m.

stops.name: Matiltan
stops.caption: It is reached by a non-metalled road in a four-wheel drive vehicle.

stops.name: Ushu (Usho)
stops.caption: The Ushu glacier blocks the only path to Mahodand in winter. It is known for its cloudy, rainy forest.

stops.name: Mahodand Lake
stops.caption: It lies about 40 km from Kalam in the Usho sub-valley. Elevation about 2,865 m.

stops.name: Kalam
stops.caption: The Swat River forms at Kalam from the Gabral and Ushu rivers.

stops.name: Utror
stops.caption: It is 16 km from Kalam. Badogai Pass connects it to Upper Dir.

stops.name: Gabral
stops.caption: The Gabral River joins the Utror River there. It is about 7 km from Utror by road and 20 km from Kalam.

stories.title: Utror to Kundol Lake by Laddu

stops.name: Kalam
stops.caption: The metalled road ends here; a shingle road continues to the Ushu and Utror valleys.

stops.name: Utror
stops.caption: The valley is surrounded by snow-clad mountains, green pastures and waterfalls. It is one of the Swat Kohistan valleys inhabited by Gawri people.

stops.name: Laddu (Utror side)
stops.caption: Ladu is reached by hiking from Utror or by four-wheeler, about two hours.

stops.name: Kundol Lake
stops.caption: Elevation 9,950 ft in the north of Utror. Only accessible in summer.

stories.title: Thal to Kala Chashma up the Kumrat valley

stops.name: Jamia Masjid Thal (wooden mosque)
stops.caption: Built of pure wood with huge pillars. Originally built 1865.

stops.name: Kumrat Valley
stops.caption: Only reachable by four-wheel vehicles. Deodar forests beside the Panjkora.

stops.name: Kumrat Waterfall
stops.caption: Several waterfalls are in Kumrat.

stops.name: Kala Chashma (Black Spring)
stops.caption: Kala Chashma (Black Spring) is in Kumrat.

stops.name: Mingora
stops.caption: Mingora is the largest city of Malakand Division. Third largest city in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, on the Swat River.

stops.name: Butkara I Stupa
stops.caption: The stupa was probably built in the 2nd century BCE, with a possible Ashokan origin. It was enlarged five times, each time by building over the previous structure.

stops.name: Swat Museum
stops.caption: A new building opened on 11 December 2014. Most holdings come from Butkara I and Odigram.

stops.name: Saidu Sharif I Stupa and Monastery
stops.caption: The sacred area has two terraces with a stupa and a monastery. The first period dates from 25 BCE to the end of the 1st century.

stops.name: Saidu Sharif
stops.caption: Hub of official buildings: Swat Museum, Saidu Baba's mausoleum, the Wali's palace and Butkara stupa remains.

stops.name: Udegram (Odigram, ancient Ora)
stops.caption: Odigram is the site of the Ghaznavid-era mosque. Hindu Shahis made their capital at Udigram.

stops.name: Ghalegay Buddha (rock relief)
stops.caption: A Buddha is carved in rock beside the road to Mingora. Ghalegay was chosen as the first capital of Swat in 1849.

stops.name: Barikot
stops.caption: Barikot lies on the middle course of the Swat River, about 20 km from Mingora. The entrance town to central Swat, with about 115,045 people.

stops.name: Bazira (Barikot Ghundai)
stops.caption: The Italian mission has excavated Bazira since 1984. Greek accounts of Alexander's 327 BCE attack are identified with Odigram (Ora) and Barikot (Bazira).

stops.name: Amluk-Dara Stupa
stops.caption: It is unprotected and damaged by treasure hunters. Described as the best example of a stupa in Swat.

stories.title: Mingora to Malam Jabba by road

stops.name: Mingora
stops.caption: Mingora is the largest city of Malakand Division.

stops.name: Manglawar (Manglor)
stops.caption: The valley lies about 9 km north-east of Mingora. Sultan Pakhal Swati founded the Kingdom of Swat with Manglawar as its capital.

stops.name: Jahanabad Buddha (Manglawar rock relief)
stops.caption: Its style is compared to 7th-8th century Tang sculpture. The head was damaged by explosives in 2007 and later restored.

stops.name: Malam Jabba Ski Resort
stops.caption: It is one of Pakistan's two ski resorts. The resort apex is 2,804 m.

stories.title: Mingora to Bahrain by road
stories.note: Mingora is in the lower pack, so this story stays inside it. Kalam and Mahodand are in the upper pack (see kalam-to-mahodand).

stops.name: Mingora
stops.caption: Mingora is the largest city of Malakand Division.

stops.name: Khwazakhela
stops.caption: Second-largest commercial centre in Swat. Draws people from Kalam, Kohistan and Shangla.

stops.name: Bahrain (Behrain)
stops.caption: The name means 'two rivers' for the Daral/Swat confluence. It is a base camp for the Daral and Saidgai lakes trail.

stops.name: Khwazakhela
stops.caption: Second-largest commercial centre in Swat. Draws people from Kalam, Kohistan and Shangla.

stops.name: Fatehpur (Swat)
stops.caption: Fatehpur is a union council of Upper Swat.

stops.name: Madyan
stops.caption: Madyan is primarily inhabited by Torwalis. The Chail and Swat valleys join at Madyan.

stops.name: Bahrain (Behrain)
stops.caption: It lies 60 km north of Mingora at 4,700 ft on the right bank of the Swat River. It is known for riverside tourist resorts and local handicrafts.
